situation: Rendering a repeatable/dynamic list of form rows (add/remove items) where each row also has free-text inputs the user types into
right_direction: Split rendering into two paths: a full DOM rebuild ONLY on structural changes (add/remove item, a change that alters which fields are visible), and a lightweight pass that only updates error text/aria-invalid on EXISTING nodes (via data-* attributes to re-find them) for every keystroke. Calling the full rebuild on every 'input' event recreates the <input> elements and silently resets cursor position / drops the keystroke the user is mid-typing.
anti_pattern: Calling the same render function that rebuilds the whole list (replaceChildren + recreate rows) from both the 'add item' handler AND the per-field 'input' handler — it looks correct in a unit test (the final value lands in state either way) and only shows up as a real bug in an actual browser, typing a multi-character value into a freshly-added row.
